source.title: Winterreise, D. 911 — No. 11 Frühlingstraum
source.edition: OpenScore Lieder transcription from IMSLP #60822; printed-edition imprint not independently established

voices.name: Voice (baritone; treble notation sounds one octave lower)

bars.description: Pickup bar 0 (one eighth note), then printed bars 1–88 once. The six poem stanzas form two written-out dream/awakening/reflection sequences; no da capo is inserted. Bars 27–43 and 71–88 have two quarter units (2/4); the remaining complete bars have three (6/8).

endpoints.basis: Windows selected from absolute-pitch inspection of the cached Commons transfer. The final window isolates the last written piano attack, not the later surface-noise cutoff; see work/schubert-winterreise-fruhlingstraum-preparation-end.png. No listening annotation is claimed.

provenance: OpenScore Lieder releases these encodings under CC0: https://github.com/OpenScore/Lieder#license-and-acknowledgement . Exact downloaded MXL bytes match the inventory SHA-256. This is voice and piano, not an orchestral arrangement; Mutopia 373 is Einsamkeit and is not used.

Source part P1 is Singstimme (one treble-clef vocal line); P2 is Pianoforte (two staves with explicitly numbered MusicXML voices). Each source voice is extracted separately. These are encoding identities, not source-separated audio or MIDI-patch-derived instruments.

The recording is Hans Duhan, baritone, with Ferdinand Foll, piano (1928): Christian Utz, ZGMTH 18/Sonderausgabe (2021), https://www.gmth.de/zeitschrift/artikel/1132.aspx . The conventional treble vocal line sounds one octave below its written pitches. The engraving labels that octave convention explicitly; no vocal lyrics are stripped.

Transposition describes the sounding pitches of this particular Commons transfer relative to the global librosa tuning estimate, not a claim about the historical performers’ selected key or original tuning. Utz footnote 73 explicitly warns that Duhan’s transferred pitch/key is particularly uncertain. Absolute piano spectra, not filenames or a global key-classifier label, determine the configured shifts.

Opening piano E5 and A3 become nominal D5 and G3: measured peaks 603.9 and 201.7 Hz (2.5–3.0 s), at global tuning +48 cents (A=452.370 Hz). Additional global shift −2 semitones; vocal line an additional −12.

engraving.music:
\transpose c bes, <<
        
        \new Staff
        <<
            \set Staff.instrumentName = "Voice (sounds 8vb)"
            \set Staff.midiInstrument = "acoustic grand"
            
            \context Staff << 
                \mergeDifferentlyDottedOn\mergeDifferentlyHeadedOn
                \context Voice = "PartPOneVoiceOne" {  \PartPOneVoiceOne }
                \new Lyrics \lyricsto "PartPOneVoiceOne" { \set stanza = "1." \PartPOneVoiceOneLyricsOne }
                >>
            >>
        \new PianoStaff
        <<
            \set PianoStaff.instrumentName = "Pianoforte"
            \set PianoStaff.midiInstrument = "acoustic grand"
            
            \context Staff = "1" << 
                \mergeDifferentlyDottedOn\mergeDifferentlyHeadedOn
                \context Voice = "PartPTwoVoiceOne" {  \voiceOne \PartPTwoVoiceOne }
                \context Voice = "PartPTwoVoiceTwo" {  \voiceTwo \PartPTwoVoiceTwo }
                >> \context Staff = "2" <<
                \mergeDifferentlyDottedOn\mergeDifferentlyHeadedOn
                \context Voice = "PartPTwoVoiceFive" {  \PartPTwoVoiceFive }
                >>
            >>
        
        >>
